source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch. 7 (An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara).

sections.heading: 1. The Vijayanagara Empire
points: The **Vijayanagara Empire** (founded **1336** by **Harihara and Bukka**, of the **Sangama dynasty**) ruled much of South India.
Capital: **Vijayanagara ('city of victory')**, on the **Tungabhadra river** — the site is at **Hampi (Karnataka)**, a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
Four dynasties ruled: **Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu**; the greatest king was **Krishnadeva Raya (Tuluva)**.

sections.heading: 2. The City — Layout and Water
points: The city was **rediscovered by Colin Mackenzie (1800)**; studied through ruins and travellers' accounts.
Impressive **fortifications** (massive walls), gateways, and the surrounding agricultural belt.
Sophisticated **water management** — the **Kamalapuram tank** and the **Hiriya canal** supplied water and irrigation.

sections.heading: 3. Royal and Sacred Centres
points: **Royal Centre:** the 'Mahanavami Dibba' (a platform for the Mahanavami/Dussehra festival), the King's audience hall, the **Lotus Mahal**, the **elephant stables**.

**Sacred Centre:** temples — the **Virupaksha temple** (dedicated to Shiva/Pampadevi) and the **Vitthala temple** (with its famous stone chariot and musical pillars); grand **gopurams (rayagopurams)**.
The **Hazara Rama temple** was probably for the royal family.

sections.heading: 4. Decline
points: The empire declined after the **Battle of Talikota (1565)**, when a coalition of the **Deccan Sultanates** defeated Vijayanagara and sacked the capital.
The city was abandoned; the Aravidu dynasty continued rule from elsewhere for a time.
The ruins at Hampi remain a testament to its grandeur.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Vijayanagara founded 1336 by Harihara and Bukka (Sangama dynasty); capital at Hampi (Tungabhadra).
Four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu; greatest king = Krishnadeva Raya.
Rediscovered by Colin Mackenzie (1800); Hampi = UNESCO site.
Virupaksha and Vitthala temples (stone chariot, musical pillars); Lotus Mahal.
Battle of Talikota (1565) = defeat by the Deccan Sultanates → decline.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Vijayanagara was founded in **1336 by Harihara and Bukka** (Sangama dynasty).
The capital is at **Hampi**, on the **Tungabhadra** river (UNESCO site).
**Krishnadeva Raya (Tuluva dynasty)** was the greatest ruler.
The **Battle of Talikota (1565)** led to its downfall (defeated by the Deccan Sultanates).
